items.body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No - VS Code Version: 1.118.1 (after upgrading from 1.112.0) - OS Version: Fedora Linux 43 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Launch VS Code normally on Wayland 2. Open the integrated terminal 3. Have some bad luck (usually after system restart or vscode update) 4. Write anything 5. Observe text rendering Expected: Terminal text renders with correct spacing and alignment. Actual: Terminal text appears garbled with incorrect spacing and glyph positioning (characters are visually misaligned / drifting). Additional Information: - Last known tested working version: 1.112.0 - Issue appeared immediately after upgrading to 1.118.1 via dnf - Only affects the integrated terminal (editor rendering appears normal) - Stops reproducing _consistently) specifically when vscode is launched with `--ozone-platform=x11` - after this, normal code launches do not have the issue most of the time. - GPU: RTX5070 (drivers up-to-date) Temporary Workarounds: - Setting `"terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration": "off"` resolves the issue - Launching with `code --disable-gpu` resolves the issue - Launching with `code --ozone-platform=x11` resolves the issue Notes: One might guess this to be a regression in the GPU-accelerated terminal rendering path (xterm.js / Electron) on Linux Wayland, likely introduced between 1.112 and 1.118.

items.title: Numpad keys not working in terminal TUI applications after 1.110 update (Electron 39 / Chromium 142 regression)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: upstream
labels.description: Issue identified as 'upstream' component related (exists outside of VS Code)

labels.name: chromium
labels.description: Issues and items related to Chromium

items.body:
## Description

After updating to VS Code 1.110.0, numpad keys (0-9, Enter, decimal, operators) are not recognized by TUI applications running inside the integrated terminal. The numpad works correctly in the terminal shell itself before launching any TUI app.

## Environment

- **VS Code Version:** 1.110.0 (system setup)
- **Commit:** 0870c2a0c7c0564e7631bfed2675573a94ba4455
- **Date:** 2026-03-04T01:20:28.863Z
- **Electron:** 39.6.0
- **Chromium:** 142.0.7444.265
- **OS:** Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200
- **Connection:** Remote SSH to Ubuntu (ARM64)
- **TUI Application:** OpenCode (opentui-based)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code 1.110.0
2. Open integrated terminal (local or Remote SSH)
3. Verify numpad keys work in the shell (they do)
4. Launch a TUI application that uses enhanced keyboard mode (e.g., OpenCode, or any bubbletea/opentui-based app)
5. Try typing numbers using the numpad
6. Observe: numpad keystrokes are completely ignored inside the TUI

## Expected Behavior

Numpad keys should be recognized by TUI applications running in the integrated terminal, as they were in VS Code 1.109.x.

## Actual Behavior

- Numpad keys work in the terminal shell before launching the TUI app
- Numpad keys are completely ignored once the TUI app is running
- Main keyboard number row works correctly inside the TUI
- The same TUI application works correctly with numpad in an external terminal (outside VS Code)

## Analysis

This appears to be related to the Chromium 142 / Electron 39 regression where numpad keys report `key: "Unidentified"` (see #283460, chromium issue 405793116). 

The normal terminal shell compensates using `keyCode` fallback, but when a TUI application activates enhanced keyboard mode (Kitty keyboard protocol / CSI u), xterm.js passes through the broken key identity from Chromium. The TUI receives `"Unidentified"` for numpad keys and drops them.

This is distinct from #283460 which covers numpad Delete in the editor. This issue specifically affects **terminal TUI applications** that use enhanced keyboard protocols.

## Related Issues

- #283460 - Numpad Delete key not working (Chromium 142 regression, editor-level)
- Chromium issue [405793116](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/405793116)
- Chromium issue [429730008](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/429730008)

<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes
<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.107.0-insider
- OS Version: Arch Linux x64
- GPU: NVIDIA (10de:2805)

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Install VS Code Insiders on Arch Linux with NVIDIA GPU
2. Run Wayland session
3. Launch `code-insiders`
4. Blank screen appears

## Description

VS Code Insiders shows a completely blank screen on launch. This is similar to the Electron regression in #230604.

The Electron 38 update changed `--ozone-platform-hint` to `auto` by default, which attempts native Wayland on NVIDIA. VA-API initialization fails and crashes the GPU process.

## Error logs (from `code-insiders --verbose`)

```
[WARNING:wayland_drm.cc(114)] Drm prime capability is not supported
libEGL warning: egl: failed to create dri2 screen
[WARNING:media/gpu/vaapi/vaapi_wrapper.cc:129] Should skip nVidia device named: nvidia-drm
[ERROR:media/gpu/vaapi/vaapi_wrapper.cc:1631] vaInitialize failed: unknown libva error
[ERROR:components/viz/service/main/viz_main_impl.cc:189] Exiting GPU process due to errors during initialization
```

## Workaround

```
code-insiders --ozone-platform=x11
```

## Expected behavior

VS Code should detect NVIDIA VA-API failure and fall back to X11 automatically, or not default to Wayland on NVIDIA systems.

## Related

- #230604 (previous Electron regression on Linux + NVIDIA)
- Electron 38 release notes: https://www.electronjs.org/blog/electron-38-0 ("default value of --ozone-platform flag changed to auto")

We plan to promote Electron 37 in the July 2025 milestone to insiders. The following tests cover some of the common UI bits that don't have smoke tests. You can download the nightly explorations builds from [here](https://builds.code.visualstudio.com/builds/exploration?released=true&dev=true) for testing.

**Testing:**

* **macOS:**
  * Enable Native Tabs (via settings: `window.nativeTabs: true`)
    - Ensure native tabs are enabled in the system preferences (System Preferences > General > Prefer tabs: "always":)
    - Launch application
    - Try opening new window from either command line (code-exploration <path-to-project>) or from the menu entry (Cmd + Shift + N)
    - Verify new window is launched as a new tab in the active instance of the application window is focused when starting from command line
    - open the code exploration application from finder or dock
    - open external terminal
    - run code-exploration
    - make sure the new window is put to foreground
  * Font rendering with non-default family name
    - Download and install `Inconsolata ExtraBold` from [font](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Inconsolata)
    - In the editor set `"editor.fontFamily": "Inconsolata ExtraBold"`
    - Confirm that the font applies and compare it with insiders

* **windows:**
  * verify maximize and restore operations work as expected when OS task bar is auto-hidden for custom titlebar
  * Verify titlebar is not clipped off when exiting fullscreen
    - Maximize VS Code window
    - Press F11 or Ctrl+K Z twice to enter/exit full screen.
    - Verify titlebar is not cropped

* **linux:**
  * Verify clicking on native menu does not crash the application 
     - Switch to native title bar `"window.titleBarStyle": "native"`
     - Click on any of the menu options `File`, `Edit` etc
     
 * **All OS:**
   * Check out the `electron-36.x.y` branch locally and verify you can run out of sources, set a breakpoint and debug using the VS Code launch configurations and VS Code debugger
